checkov.note: Isolated uv tool. Never a project dependency (PLAN.md Q3). checkov 3.3.12 declares no console_scripts entry point (its dist-info carries no entry_points.txt, only the wheel data scripts Scripts/checkov and Scripts/checkov.cmd), so neither uv nor pip can generate a checkov.exe trampoline on any platform. Upstream's own checkov.cmd resolves `python` from PATH rather than from the tool venv, which on a Windows host carrying the Microsoft Store app-execution alias runs the stub (observed: exit 9009, 'Python was not found'). `script` is therefore the script uv places in the tool venv's Scripts dir, and `exe` is the pinned launcher bootstrap.ps1 generates into tools/bin/ around the tool venv's own interpreter.
checkov.exe_sha256_exemption: Deliberate, not an oversight: the two github-release entries carry exe_sha256 and this one cannot. checkov's `exe` is a .cmd that bootstrap.ps1 generates, embedding this host's absolute interpreter path, so its hash is host-specific and changes legitimately on every machine - pinning it would fail everywhere but the machine it was recorded on. checkov's integrity rests instead on four other things; see the exemption comment in tools/bootstrap.ps1's Install-UvTool for the full reasoning.

tfsec.note: Last upstream release 2025-05-02, 15 months before capture. Retained as legacy/comparative per PLAN.md R1-#19. The .exe asset publishes only a GPG .sig, so the checksummed .tar.gz is used instead. The tarball also contains tfsec-checkgen.exe, which this framework never runs; `exe` names tfsec.exe explicitly rather than globbing, so checkgen deliberately gets no entry and no exe_sha256.
